items: Both work with network/franchise models: Gershon has worked with franchise prospects (Franchise 2017/2018 events).

lead_with.title: The Sun Belt construction boom
lead_with.text: European projects in the US are moving south: **+46% Texas, +51% Florida** (Barometer 2026, as Olivier wrote on Oct 8). These are the busiest US residential and light-construction markets.

lead_with.title: US contractors already buy small loads
lead_with.text: Small US contractors and DIY buyers rely on bagged mix or short-load trucks with minimum-load fees. A 24/7 self-service dispenser solves that (US competitors and pricing **to be confirmed**).

lead_with.title: Partner model, low capex
lead_with.text: Ask whether he would go US via **building-material dealers or franchisees** hosting machines rather than owning sites. Gershon can find and qualify those partners.

lead_with.title: Start with a test market
lead_with.text: Propose a 3-month market test: ICP, 10 qualified meetings a month with dealers / ready-mix players in Texas or Florida.

The company was founded by **François Behr**. Le Journal des Entreprises also ran a piece on SELFBETON "launching several avenues to develop its activity" (content not accessible). His background before SELFBETON is **not verified**; a possible link to the Mathis construction family group in Alsace is **not confirmed** and should not be raised.

company.text: SELFBETON runs **self-service concrete dispensers** open to professionals and the public. Customers pick a mix (up to **50** depending on the site), pay at a kiosk, then scan a **QR-code ticket**; the machine loads the concrete into their trailer or truck. This avoids buying cement, sand and gravel separately or waiting for a mixer truck. In 2022 it had **almost 40 dispensers** in Normandy, Brittany, Ile-de-France and Occitanie, with new sites such as **Pédernec** (Brittany). It planned online pre-payment. The company is listed as a **Moselle** BTP firm. Prices were about **€15-20 above** usual market rates (2022), paid for by convenience.

industry.title: US housing shortage
industry.text: The US needs millions of new homes; Texas and Florida lead permits. Small contractors are a big buyer group.

industry.title: Short-load pain
industry.text: US ready-mix suppliers often charge short-load fees for small orders. That is the gap self-service fills.

industry.title: Volumetric trucks compete
industry.text: Volumetric mixer trucks and bagged mix are the current US alternatives.

industry.title: Local permits
industry.text: Concrete plants need local environmental and zoning permits; partners with existing yards make it faster.

talking_points: How many dispensers are running today, and what is the target for 2027?
Who is your best customer: small builders, landscapers, farmers, or DIY?
Have you been approached by foreign partners or distributors already?
Would you sell machines, franchise sites, or operate them yourself in the US?
Which state interests you: Texas, Florida, or elsewhere?
What budget and timeline would you give a US test?
